instruction: Design the main screen (a single page) for a Magic Academy learning game. Include an atmospheric academy hall or study scene, a student profile with rank and progress, a curriculum of magical course cards, a prominent current lesson, an upcoming exam panel, spell mastery indicators, and one clear Learn or Practice action. Put strong emphasis on an enchanting scholarly identity, readable progression, meaningful card differentiation, elegant typography, and polished visual craft.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: Two required modules are absent from the visible screen — there is no curriculum of magical course cards (the 'CURRICULUM' nav item leads nowhere on-page) and no spell mastery indicators (same for 'MASTERY'). The brief's emphasis on 'meaningful card differentiation' therefore fails entirely, since zero cards exist. The 'atmospheric academy hall or study' is only implied by an abstract teal orb and floating glyphs; there is no architecture, depth, candlelight, or scholarly props, so it reads as a widget, not a place. The single clear Learn/Practice action is clipped at the viewport bottom (only a blue sliver shows), so the one action the brief demands is not actually visible or usable in this frame. Clarity & Hierarchy: The 'prominent current lesson' is demoted to the second slot in the left column and is cut off, while the poetic 'LIVE / The Convergence is steady' scene copy competes with it for the eye. The exam panel repeats '82%' twice (inline and right-aligned), and the countdown highlights only the minutes in blue with no stated logic, muddying what the numbers mean. The three stat tiles (1,214 / 37 / 6) sit as equal boxes with no clear primary. Visual System & Craft: The base system is strong and coherent — deep navy, gold + teal accents, an elegant Didone-style display face, monospace micro-labels, corner-bracket framing, and a clean gold XP gradient. But there is jank: the lesson card and its CTA overflow the fold, the exam's secondary button is also clipped, and the inconsistent countdown coloring breaks an otherwise precise palette. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The orb, glyph field, and italic-gold word treatments ('Convergence', 'Alchemical') are genuinely authored moments, but the overall composition is a conventional dark dashboard; the 'enchanting scholarly identity' is carried mostly by type color rather than by environment, texture, or a distinctive layout, so it risks reading as a generic fantasy template once the missing content is filled in. Real trade-off: adding course cards + mastery will raise vertical density and risk pushing the already-clipped CTA further below the fold, so the grid must be restructured, not just appended to.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all CSS/SVG, no external assets): 1) Restore the two omitted modules to satisfy the brief. Add a 'Curriculum' row of 3–4 differentiated course cards (e.g., Transmutation, Runecraft, Aetheric Theory, Bestiary), each with its own sigil icon, difficulty tag, a progress ring, and a distinct status (in-progress / available / locked) so differentiation is legible at a glance. Add a compact 'Spell Mastery' module — a grid of spell sigils each with a 5-pip or ring mastery level and a 'practiced this week' tick. 2) Fix the clipped primary action and re-rank the grid so the lesson's single gold CTA ('Continue — Rite 3 of 5') is fully visible above the fold and is the most prominent control on the page; demote the exam's button to a ghost/secondary style. Re-flow to a 12-col layout: left rail = compact scene + mastery; center = lesson (CTA visible) + course-card row; right = profile + exam. 3) Upgrade the scene from an isolated orb into a full-width atmospheric header band behind the top nav and profile — gothic arches, warm candle glow at the edges, drifting glyphs, a soft vignette — keeping the orb as the focal 'resonance' element but adding depth cues so it reads as a hall/study; trim the scene's text to one caption so it stops competing with the lesson title. 4) Tighten hierarchy and consistency: make all countdown digits one color (emphasize only the active unit subtly), remove the duplicated 82%, give the three stat tiles a clear primary (Total XP) with quieter secondaries, and ensure the 'LIVE' tag is a small status, not a headline. 5) Polish pass: add hover/active/focus states to cards and buttons, verify no clipping at 1280px, and confirm the gold CTA, teal secondary, and navy surfaces form one consistent state system.

- The atmospheric scene vs. information density: a full hall scene costs space. Resolution: turn the scene into a slim full-width header backdrop (arches, candlelight, floating glyphs) that sits behind the top bar/profile, so atmosphere is present without stealing a whole column.
- CTA clarity: ensure the single primary action ("Continue Lesson" / "Practice") is the most prominent element, above the fold, with the exam's secondary action clearly subordinate.

Prioritized revision plan:
1. Restore missing required content: add a "Curriculum" section with 3–4 differentiated course cards (e.g., Transmutation, Runecraft, Aetheric Theory, Bestiary) each with distinct icon, difficulty, progress ring, and status (locked/in-progress/complete) to satisfy "meaningful card differentiation." Add a "Spell Mastery" module — a compact grid of spell sigils with mastery levels (e.g., 5 pips or a ring), placed in the left column under the scene or as a horizontal strip.
2. Fix the clipped CTA: restructure the grid so the lesson card's primary button ("Continue — Rite 3 of 5") is fully visible above the fold; make it the single dominant gold button; demote the exam's button to a ghost/secondary.
3. Elevate the scene into an environmental header: replace the isolated orb widget with a full-width atmospheric band (gothic arches, candle glow, drifting glyphs, subtle vignette) behind the top nav and profile, keeping the orb as a focal "resonance" element but adding depth cues so it reads as a hall/study.
4. Tighten hierarchy and consistency: unify countdown number colors (all one color, emphasize only the active unit subtly), remove the duplicated 82%, group the three stat tiles with clearer labels, and ensure the "LIVE" scene copy doesn't compete with the lesson title — reduce scene text to a single caption.
5. Polish: add hover/active states to cards and buttons, ensure focus rings, and verify no clipping at 1280px.

Keep it offline/self-contained: all via CSS/SVG, no external assets.

The information hierarchy is muddled by a 'three-column tug-of-war': the 'Spell Mastery' panel on the left competes visually with the 'Upcoming Examination' on the right, neither of which is the primary focus, while the 'Current Lesson' in the center lacks sufficient visual dominance to act as the clear focal point. Furthermore, the 'Learn or Practice' action is split between a 'Continue' button and a 'Review Notes' button, diluting the single clear call-to-action requested in the brief. The atmospheric background is too dark and static, failing to provide the 'enchanting' scholarly identity requested, and the gold accents, while elegant, are applied somewhat indiscriminately to borders and text, reducing their impact as a premium highlight.
